takeaway: Splenectomy is done for unstable or high-grade splenic injury, ITP, hereditary spherocytosis and autoimmune haemolytic anaemia; not for sickle cell disease sequestration, where transfusion is preferred.

question.text: Splenectomy is indicated for all but which one of the following conditions?

lines.text: We are looking for the one condition where the spleen stays in.
If the injury is greater than grade three, or the patient becomes unstable, the spleen comes out.
Idiopathic thrombocytopenic purpura is a classic indication.
So is hereditary spherocytosis, with its round fragile red cells.
And so is autoimmune haemolytic anaemia.
But in sickle cell disease, there is little evidence for splenectomy during an acute sequestration crisis.
A blood transfusion is preferred instead, so sickle cell disease is the exception.
lines.say: A blood transfusion is preferred instead. (sigh) So sickle cell disease is the exception.
